test_quote_freshness.py.rationale: Change B adds Catalog.quote, which returns the total of a basket at current prices, and its docstring builds on Catalog.price returning 'the current price'. Change A makes price() keep every value it has read, with no invalidation. On the merged tree, quote therefore reuses stale cached prices after the backend price changes, so the basket total is wrong (800 instead of 1000). These tests pass on B alone, fail on base and on A because quote is missing, and fail on the merge because of the stale cache.

test_quote_repeats.py.rationale: Change B's core intent is that a SKU listed twice counts twice. On the merged tree, quote goes through A's cache, so repeated SKUs get their price from the cache rather than the backend. This test checks that the duplicate counting still holds when part of the basket is already cached.

test_price_cache_reads.py.rationale: Change A's intent is that repeated lookups of a SKU read the slow backend once, even when several SKUs are looked up in an interleaved order. A cart page that totals a basket does exactly this. The test uses only price(), so it can run on the A tree. It confirms that on the merged tree the cache still limits backend reads to one per distinct SKU.
